clue.text: Conflict about iron takes the biscuit

indicators.note: about means one word is placed around the other here

parts.note: a conflict between nations is a war
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A row over iron is the last straw, the one that takes the biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes the biscuit' reads as the idiom for outrageousness, but only 'biscuit' defines; 'about' puts WAR around FE.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin crisp wafer is a kind of biscuit eaten with ice cream.

clue.text: To retire is not unattractive

definitions.meaning: a cryptic reading: possessing pulling power

explanation.surface: Going into retirement is not without its appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word into two: having a draw, that is, having appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire is to pull back or leave, and having appeal is jokingly having a draw.

clue.text: Sack member for having a weapon

parts.note: to sack is to fire from a job
an arm is a limb, or member, of the body

explanation.surface: An employee was dismissed for carrying a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' and 'member' read as dismissing a club member; they are FIRE and ARM.
explanation.definitionFit: A firearm is a gun, a kind of weapon.

clue.text: Not a counterfeit coin

explanation.surface: A coin that is genuine, not forged.
explanation.walkthrough: The real was an old Spanish coin; the plural is reales.
explanation.definitionFit: Genuine means authentic rather than fake, and a former Spanish and Brazilian currency bears the same name.

clue.text: Appeared to have caused embarrassment

definitions.meaning: turned up, arrived on the scene
made someone look foolish or exposed them

explanation.surface: Someone arrived and promptly made a scene that embarrassed others.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both arrived somewhere and humiliated a person by outshining or exposing them.

clue.text: Hero left her all confused very, very quickly

indicators.note: confused means the letters of hero left her all are jumbled

explanation.surface: A muddled hero abandoned her in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means at breakneck speed, as fast as possible.

clue.text: Initially work a long time to earn it

indicators.note: initially means just the opening letter of work is used

parts.note: an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: You start work and put in years before you get paid.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads loosely as the thing you work to earn, with 'it' standing for pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Pay received for labour is what you work to earn.

clue.text: Do boil a stew if it's game

indicators.note: stew as a verb asks for the letters of do boil a to be mixed up

explanation.surface: Cooking instructions: boil and stew it if it is game meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' looks like hunted meat to stew; it is a juggling toy game, a spool spun on a string between two sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: Diabolo is a toy and pastime in which a spinning spool is tossed on a string between sticks.

clue.text: He offers services to servicemen

parts.note: religious services offered to soldiers and sailors by a military chaplain

explanation.surface: Someone who provides help to members of the armed forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'services' reads as help; it means church services, held for the forces.
explanation.definitionFit: A military chaplain leads worship for troops, and soldiers call him by this nickname.

clue.text: Destitute mason needs bone transplant

indicators.note: transplant suggests the letters of mason needs bone are moved into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A broke stonemason requires a bone graft.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, from a ship heeled over on its side, means in desperate financial straits.

clue.text: Country suite to take in Her Majesty

indicators.note: to take in means one piece swallows the other, so the second sits inside the first

parts.note: a suite is a retinue of attendants, which is also a train
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: Royal staff in a country retreat must make room for the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' looks like a nation; here it means land or landscape. ER is the late Queen's royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: Country in the sense of open land or ground is a synonym of the landscape's type.

clue.text: Convict has to pull back when he trails behind

parts.note: an old lag is a convict

indicators.note: back, following pull, tells us the word for pull is read in reverse

parts.note: to pull is to drag

explanation.surface: A prisoner has to haul back when he falls behind the others.
explanation.walkthrough: LAG is British slang for a convict, as in 'old lag'.
explanation.definitionFit: A straggler who falls behind the rest is a dawdler, someone slow.

clue.text: A bargain from Kentish town

definitions.meaning: an agreement or transaction struck between parties
a seaside town on the coast of Kent, England

explanation.surface: Picking up a bargain from a shop in a Kent town.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal is a coastal town in Kent, south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargain is an agreement struck, and the Kent port is a place name shared with that word.

clue.text: What the nicotine addict may take to stop the candle smoking

definitions.text: What the nicotine addict may take
definitions.meaning: powdered tobacco sniffed up the nose
put out a flame by pinching or capping the wick

explanation.surface: A smoker's habit set against putting out a candle.
explanation.definitionFit: Powdered tobacco is taken by sniffing, and to extinguish a wick is also expressed by the same word.

clue.text: Ambassador has to take in enormous breeches

indicators.note: to take in means the first piece holds the second within it

parts.note: an ambassador is addressed as His Excellency, abbreviated HE
OS stands for outsize, a clothing label for very large garments

explanation.surface: A diplomat has to let out his huge trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take in' is tailoring talk for narrowing clothes, which fits the breeches, but here it means containing.
explanation.definitionFit: Hose in the historical sense were close-fitting leg coverings, the old equivalent of breeches or tights.

clue.text: One plea to party dissidents!

parts.note: the call a leader makes to rebels within a political party: stick together

explanation.surface: A political leader appeals to rebels in the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' also hints at the meaning, being one in oneness.
explanation.definitionFit: Togetherness or oneness is the cry to factions in a split party.

clue.text: Lay down a condition

definitions.meaning: to declare formally or set out

explanation.surface: Setting out terms of an agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare or set out formally is one sense, and a condition or situation is the other.

clue.text: Government somehow isn't held in high regard

indicators.note: held in means the rearranged letters are placed inside the longer word

parts.note: high regard is admiration

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of isn't are put together in some other order

explanation.surface: Ministers are, for some reason, not well thought of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' makes NIST from ISN'T, and 'held in' places it inside ADMIRATION, between ADMI and RATION.
explanation.definitionFit: The administration is the group running the country, the executive in power.

clue.text: Proposal about to finish off the criminal

indicators.note: about means the first word goes around the second

parts.note: a proposal is an offer
to finish off is to end

explanation.surface: An offer is made to finish off the crook.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawbreaker is one who has committed a crime.

clue.text: Don't buy an object that is worse or worst

definitions.text: Don't buy an object that is worse
definitions.meaning: a cryptic reading: acquire the superior of two items
as a verb, to defeat or overcome someone

explanation.surface: Shopping advice: pick the superior item rather than the poorer one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worst' looks like an adjective at the end of the comparison; it is a verb meaning to defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: To worst someone is to beat or outdo them, the same as overcoming them in a contest.

clue.text: Typical example of chapter taken from epic book

indicators.note: taken from means the letter is removed from the word epic

parts.note: a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: A chapter extracted from an epic book serves as a classic case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken from' looks like quoting a passage, but it removes C from EPIC, leaving EPI.
explanation.definitionFit: The epitome is the perfect embodiment, the quintessential instance of a type.

clue.text: Army men certain to come back

parts.note: RE are the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
bound means certain, as in bound to happen

explanation.surface: Soldiers are sure to return.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring back after hitting something is to return.

clue.text: Cry out against a laid-back perjurer

indicators.note: laid-back tells us the word for perjurer is laid down backwards

parts.note: a perjurer is a liar under oath

explanation.surface: Protesting against a relaxed witness who lies in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid-back' looks like it means relaxed, but it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail is to complain or protest bitterly, to inveigh against something.

clue.text: Umpire takes it for a major overhaul

parts.note: a ref, or referee, is an umpire

explanation.surface: The match official gets the blame for a big repair job.
explanation.definitionFit: A refit is a renovation, especially of a ship, re-equipping it thoroughly.

clue.text: It may be formed through friendship

indicators.note: be formed suggests the letters of it may are shaped into a new word

explanation.surface: A bond that may grow out of being friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be formed' rearranges the letters of IT MAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Amity is friendly relations, goodwill between people or nations.

clue.text: Clever Labour leader in Lincoln

indicators.note: in means the letter goes inside the president's name

parts.note: Abraham Lincoln is familiarly called Abe

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of Labour is taken

explanation.surface: A smart Labour Party chief based in the city of Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lincoln' reads as the English cathedral city, but it is Abe Lincoln, the US president.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever and capable both describe someone skilled and competent.

clue.text: Grime leads to upset stomachs

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the word for stomachs upside down

parts.note: tums is a colloquial word for stomachs

explanation.surface: Dirt causes stomach upsets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset stomachs' reads as indigestion; 'upset' reverses TUMS in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Smut is soot or a flake of dirt, a smudge of grime.

clue.text: A crystal box

definitions.meaning: a crystalline mineral that splits easily
to box is to ..., to fight with fists

explanation.surface: A crystal container.
explanation.definitionFit: Spar is a cleavable crystalline mineral such as feldspar, and to spar is to practise boxing.

clue.text: He serves a chiropodist

definitions.meaning: a liveried servant in a grand house
a cryptic reading: a man who deals with feet

explanation.surface: A servant waiting on a foot doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A liveried household servant is one who waits on others, and a foot specialist is jokingly a man for feet.

clue.text: Point out clearly that Sterling's gone!

parts.note: gone means former, which is ex
the pound is the unit of sterling currency

explanation.surface: Explaining plainly that the British currency has vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: EX, from 'gone' (former), is placed before POUND.
explanation.definitionFit: To expound is to explain in detail, to set out a point clearly.

clue.text: Dissertation in which I restate position

indicators.note: position used as a verb asks for the letters of I restate to be placed differently

explanation.surface: A thesis in which the author restates a stance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'position' looks like the stance being restated; it is the anagram signal on I RESTATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A treatise is a formal written study of a subject, like a thesis.

clue.text: It reflects aircraft movement this way and that

indicators.note: this way and that says the word reads the same in either direction

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A device that bounces signals off planes in flight.
explanation.definitionFit: Radar sends out radio waves that bounce off planes, tracking where they go.
